landing.faq.stack.question: What's the tech stack?
landing.faq.stack.answer: Next.js 16 with the App Router, React 19, TypeScript strict mode, Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn/ui, Drizzle ORM, and better-auth. Every piece of business logic is inlined — no external packages for payment, email, storage, or AI.
landing.faq.payment.question: Which payment providers are supported?
landing.faq.payment.answer: Stripe, PayPal, Creem, Alipay, and WeChat Pay out of the box. The PaymentManager abstraction makes it straightforward to add more providers by implementing a single interface.
landing.faq.database.question: Which databases can I use?
landing.faq.database.answer: Drizzle ORM handles PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, Turso, and Cloudflare D1. Switch providers by editing DATABASE_PROVIDER in your .env — the schema templates and drizzle config adapt automatically.
landing.faq.customize.question: How customizable is the landing page?
landing.faq.customize.answer: The src/blocks/ directory ships with demo sections — they're designed to be rewritten per project. The durable primitives live in src/components/, so your rebrand touches blocks and translations, not the chassis.
landing.faq.license.question: Can I use this for commercial projects?
landing.faq.license.answer: Yes. ShipAny Next is built for shipping production SaaS products. You own the code after cloning — no per-seat fees, no runtime dependencies on our infrastructure.

face.about_title: What is a square face icon generator?
face.about_description: A square face icon generator lets you build a pixel character by choosing its colors and features. Here, you start with a ready-made face instead of a blank canvas. Choose a skin tone, hair color, outfit and background, then change the hairstyle, expression or glasses. Every change appears in the preview, so you can keep trying combinations without drawing anything yourself.
face.about_use: The finished icon is a square 256×256 PNG. Use it as a profile picture, a character placeholder for a game project, or a small signature for your posts. The circular preview shows how the same face looks inside a round profile frame. Pick a transparent background when you want the icon to sit on your own design.
face.how_title: How to use the square face generator
face.step1_description: Begin with skin and hair colors, then select an outfit that is easy to distinguish from the background. Pick a preset or use Custom color for your own shade. The Hairstyle menu includes short cuts, curls, ponytails, buns and a bald option. Choose an expression, then try eyewear or facial hair if you like. To make a recognizable profile picture, focus on details such as your hairstyle, glasses or favorite color. You can revisit any choice as you work.
face.step2_description: Look at the large square preview and the small circular preview after each change. A face that looks good at full size may feel crowded when cropped, so check that the hair and expression are still recognizable. If the palette feels too similar, change the outfit or background to create more contrast. Use Surprise me when you want a different direction, then adjust the result rather than starting every choice from scratch. Try a few combinations before deciding which one to save.
face.step3_description: Choose a solid background for a complete icon, or select Transparent when you need a cutout. Click Download 256×256 PNG and keep the file in a folder you can find later. Before refreshing the page, save any other color versions you want to compare. Open the downloaded file to check the final result, then upload it to your profile or import it into your project. If you need a larger PNG, use the pixel art resizer with an integer multiplier to preserve the crisp edges.
face.ideas_eyebrow: A starting point for your next character
face.idea1_description: Pair brown hair with an orange outfit and a cream background. Try a smile and glasses for a friendly profile icon that is easy to recognize at a small size.
face.idea2_description: Combine purple hair, a yellow outfit and a pink background. Spiky hair and a surprised expression give the character a lively look for a chat or gaming profile.
face.idea3_description: Give your friends the same outfit color or background, then choose different hair and expressions for each person. Download each face separately to make a coordinated set.
face.related_title: Keep creating with your square face icon
face.related_description: Resize a downloaded icon without blurring its pixels, make a craft grid, or turn a different image into pixel art.
face.faq1_q: Is this square face generator free?
face.faq1_a: Yes. All avatar controls and PNG downloads shown on this page are free to use. You do not need an account, a subscription or a payment to create and save your square face icon. Try different combinations and download the versions you like. Features described elsewhere as future plans are separate from the working avatar maker you see here.
face.faq2_q: Can I use the square face generator on mobile?
face.faq2_a: Yes. Open this page in a current browser on your phone or tablet. The avatar preview and download buttons appear before the controls on small screens, so you can see your result without navigating to another page. Tap the color swatches, choose a hairstyle or expression, then save the PNG. If you cannot find the saved image, check your browser or device Downloads folder. No app installation is required.
face.faq3_a: The main address of this site is the English version, with English avatar controls, instructions and FAQs. A Chinese version is available through the language switcher in the menu. Switching languages opens the corresponding page, so save your current PNG first if you want to keep that design. The artwork and available controls are the same in both languages.
face.faq4_q: What can I download? Can the background be transparent?
face.faq4_a: You can download a 256×256 PNG. Select Transparent from the background colors before saving if you want the background to remain clear. The image is enlarged from a 32×32 pixel design without smoothing, so its blocky edges stay sharp. Use a solid color when you prefer a ready-to-upload profile picture, or transparency when you plan to place the character over your own artwork.
face.faq5_q: Is this the original square face generator from Flash Museum?
face.faq5_a: This page is an independent avatar maker with original pixel shapes. It does not run the classic Flash file. Flash Museum lists the archived Square Face Icon Generator as a 2013 release by h071019; the archive link below takes you to that separate tool. Use the controls above for this browser-based maker, or follow the archive link if you specifically want the classic version. This site is not affiliated with Flash Museum or Flashpoint.
face.classic_link: View the classic generator on Flash Museum
face.faq6_q: Is this square face generator part of Picrew?
face.faq6_a: No. This tool is independent and is not hosted on or affiliated with Picrew. You can build a square pixel character here using the colors, hairstyles, expressions and glasses shown above. If a tutorial or shared image points to a particular Picrew maker, its available parts may differ from this page. Use the preview here to check the design you can actually create before downloading.
face.faq7_q: Can I use my avatar as a profile picture or in a project?
face.faq7_a: Yes. The original avatar designs made with this tool can be used in personal or commercial projects. The PNG can serve as a profile picture, game portrait or starting point for a craft pattern. Check the final crop or display size in the project where you use it. If you add external artwork, logos or other materials later, those additions have their own permissions to consider.
face.cta_title: Make a square face that feels like you.
face.cta_description: Start with the face above, try a few colors and save your favorite. Your next profile icon is a few choices away.
face.features_title: What you can make with this avatar maker
face.feature1_description: Start with 12 skin tones and 16 preset colors each for hair, outfit and background, plus transparency for the background. The Custom color picker lets you choose your own shade for each area. Combine 12 hairstyles and 10 expressions with four eyewear styles and three facial hair styles, or leave those accessories off. A single color change can shift the mood of the whole face. Each choice works independently, so changing your hair does not reset the rest of the design.
face.feature2_title: See square and circular previews together
face.feature2_description: The large preview shows the square artwork, and the smaller preview shows its circular crop. Use both to check the face before saving, especially if your profile picture will appear in a round frame. Surprise me picks a combination of the available colors and features. It gives you a starting point when you have no particular character in mind; afterward, the same controls let you change any detail you want to keep or replace.
face.feature3_title: Save a sharp PNG with a clear background
face.feature3_description: Your character is drawn on a 32×32 pixel canvas and exported as a 256×256 PNG. Each source pixel becomes a sharp eight-pixel square, with smoothing turned off. Select Transparent from the background colors if you want to place the face over another image. A colored background is useful when you want a finished profile icon without extra editing. You can download several versions and compare them before choosing the one to use.
face.feature4_description: You do not need to upload a selfie, install drawing software or create an account to use this page. The avatar is drawn locally in your browser from the selected character parts. Desktop controls sit beside the preview; on a small phone screen, the preview and download buttons appear above them. Save a PNG before leaving or refreshing the page, because the current avatar choices are not stored as a saved project.
face.cases_title: Four ways to use your square face icon
face.cases_description: A small character can work across profiles, games and physical projects. Start with the same downloaded PNG, then adapt the background, crop or grid to the place where you want to use it.
face.case1_description: Create a face that your friends can recognize in a busy conversation. Choose a distinctive hair color, expression or pair of glasses, and check the small circular preview before downloading. Discord often displays profile pictures much smaller than the original file, so a simple color combination can be easier to read than several similar shades. Save the PNG, then choose it as your profile image in Discord. You can make matching avatars for a group by keeping the outfit or background color consistent.
face.case1_tip: For a quick check, step back from the screen and see whether the eyes and hair still stand out in the round preview. Try a solid background if your transparent face blends into the interface. Keep several versions so you can compare them in your actual profile.
face.case2_title: A game sprite or character portrait
face.case2_description: Use the character as a static sprite, an NPC portrait, a player badge or a placeholder while you develop a game. A transparent PNG is convenient when you want the face to sit over a menu or scene. The artwork starts as a 32×32 design, but the downloadable file is 256×256. Import it at a suitable display size and choose point or nearest-neighbor filtering in your editor or engine to avoid softening the pixel edges.
face.case2_tip: If your project needs a native 32×32 asset, reduce the PNG with nearest-neighbor sampling in an image editor. For a larger version, use the resizer linked below. Animate the character or draw additional poses separately in your sprite editor; this generator exports one still image at a time.
face.case3_description: Make a consistent visual identity for your social profiles, community accounts or a personal blog. Start with a face and palette you like, then save the same icon for each account. The square file works as a starting point for profile uploads, while the circular preview helps you check how a round crop will affect the result. A colored background gives the avatar a clear boundary; transparency lets you add your own backdrop later in an image editor.
face.case3_tip: Check the crop offered by each platform before confirming the upload. Leave the eyes and mouth easy to see, and test the icon at a small size. If you make separate personal and gaming accounts, change one accent color while keeping the same hair and expression to connect the two designs.
face.case4_title: A bead, cross-stitch or mosaic pattern
face.case4_description: Turn your avatar into a small craft project. First download the face as a PNG, then open the pixel art pattern maker linked below and upload that file. Start with a 32-pixel grid to follow the original design, and choose a small palette so there are fewer materials to match. The pattern tool creates numbered cells and a color inventory. Download the grid, or use Print / save PDF to keep a printable version with the color counts.
face.case4_tip: Choose a solid background if every cell should be filled. Match the listed RGB colors to the beads or threads you own before starting: the current inventory uses generic colors rather than manufacturer codes. For a first attempt, use a simple hairstyle and a few contrasting colors so the face is easy to follow on the grid.
face.case4_link: Turn your avatar into a craft grid
face.faq8_q: How do I make a cute square face avatar?
face.faq8_a: Try a smile or happy expression with a warm outfit and a soft background. Long hair, purple hair or glasses can add a detail that makes the face feel more personal. Keep some contrast between the hair and background so the small icon stays readable. The three ideas above offer starting palettes, but you can also use Surprise me and adjust the combination that catches your eye.
face.faq9_q: Can I make an original character with this tool?
face.faq9_a: You can combine the available parts into a character of your own choosing. Use colors, hair and expression to establish a personality, then save the result before trying another direction. Because everyone chooses from the same set of parts, another person could make the same combination. You can develop a more distinctive character by adding custom details afterward in an image editor.
face.faq10_q: Does the square face generator work on Chrome?
face.faq10_a: Yes. The maker uses standard browser canvas drawing and PNG downloads, and works in current Chrome with JavaScript enabled. There is no Flash plugin to install. Change a color to check the live preview, then press the download button to save the image. If a download is missing, check Chrome’s download list and any browser message about saving files. Refresh only after saving a version you want to keep.
face.faq11_q: Is the result pixel art, and why is it 256×256?
face.faq11_a: Yes. The face is made from square pixels on a 32×32 canvas. The PNG export enlarges each pixel by a factor of eight, giving a 256×256 file while keeping the same amount of design detail. This makes the blocks easier to display without blur. When resizing again, use nearest-neighbor sampling and integer scale factors where possible to keep those edges clear.

entry.icon.title: Free Square Face Icon Generator – Make a Pixel Icon
entry.icon.intro: Create a square pixel face icon with a clear silhouette, simple colors and a readable expression. Start with a blue, glasses-wearing character, adjust the details below, and download a PNG for your profile, project or small interface.
entry.icon.about_title: Design a face that works at icon size
entry.icon.about1: A square face icon generator is useful when a character needs to remain recognizable in a compact space. The face, hairstyle and glasses provide the main identifying shapes; a restrained background helps separate those shapes from the surrounding interface. This entry starts with square glasses and a cool blue palette so you can judge the outline before adding more personality.
entry.icon.about2: Use the large square preview to check the overall balance and the circular preview to check whether the face survives a rounded crop. The underlying artwork uses a 32 by 32 pixel grid and downloads as a 256 by 256 PNG. Larger output preserves the block shapes; it does not add extra facial detail.

alternative.h1: Picrew Alternative for Quick Square Avatars
alternative.eyebrow: A shorter path to a pixel profile picture
alternative.intro: Need a square pixel avatar and a downloadable file? Start with the character below, choose your colors and expression, and export a PNG without an account. This Picrew alternative focuses on one practical workflow: a ready-made face, square-first previews and a direct download.
alternative.disclosure: This guide is published by the team behind this square face generator. It explains our own tool and selected Picrew workflows; the two services are independent.
alternative.position_title: An alternative for a specific job: a square pixel PFP
alternative.position1: Searching for a Picrew alternative can mean several different things. You might want a quick profile picture, a particular illustration style, a character with specific accessories, or a place to publish your own image maker. This page addresses the first of those needs: making a simple square pixel face and leaving with a usable file. Decide whether that visual style fits your project before comparing individual buttons or colors.
alternative.position2: Picrew describes image makers built from selectable parts, with both dress-up and random formats. That variety is useful when the maker itself is part of what you want to discover. Here, the starting decision is already made: one pixel portrait editor is available on the page. Choose this route when you already know you want a square pixel avatar and prefer to spend your attention adjusting the character instead of choosing a maker.
alternative.benefit1_title: Start with a character already on the canvas
alternative.benefit1_body: The editor opens with a complete face rather than an empty canvas. Hair, skin, outfit and background already work together, so you can change only the choices that matter to you. Begin with a hairstyle and expression, then decide whether to add glasses or facial hair. Random can suggest a different combination when you need inspiration. Quick start describes the number of decisions before editing; it is not a measured claim that this site loads faster than every Picrew maker.
alternative.benefit2_title: Keep the square composition from the beginning
alternative.benefit2_body: The native character is drawn on a 32 by 32 pixel grid, and the download is a 256 by 256 square PNG. You do not need to decide on a separate canvas shape before creating the face. The square preview shows the complete portrait, while the round preview helps you inspect a circular profile crop. This is useful for an account tile, a member card or a chat avatar. The downloaded file stays square even when a destination platform displays it inside a circle.
alternative.benefit3_title: Download the PNG from the editor
alternative.benefit3_body: When the preview looks right, use the PNG download button beside the character. Choose a solid background for a self-contained profile image, or select transparency when you want to place the face on your own card or scene. The export enlarges the pixel artwork with hard edges, so you can keep the deliberate block shapes. Save the file itself rather than taking a screenshot of the preview; screenshots can introduce an unwanted background, crop or display scaling.
alternative.benefit4_body: The current public avatar editor lets you adjust the character and download the result without signing up or logging in. No email confirmation or saved-project setup is part of this export flow. That is convenient for a one-off avatar, especially when you just want a file for another service. Keep your downloaded versions on your device: this editor does not provide a cloud project library, a character history or an undo stack for earlier random results.
alternative.compare_title: Compare the workflow, not a whole platform
alternative.compare_intro: Use this table to match the task you have today. The Picrew column summarizes selected official help pages, not every creator’s maker. A feature may vary with the maker or account function you choose. The advantage here is a predictable route to one kind of output, rather than a promise to replace the range of experiences on Picrew.

alternative.step1_body: Begin with the features someone should recognize in a small thumbnail. A familiar hairstyle and a clear expression usually give you a useful starting direction. Add square glasses, round glasses or a visor only if they help the character you have in mind. You can preview each choice immediately; there is no separate completion page between ordinary edits. If you use Random, download an interesting result before asking for another one, because the next combination replaces the current character.
alternative.step2_title: Match the palette and check both previews
alternative.step2_body: Choose skin, hair and outfit colors before settling on the background. A little contrast between hair and background makes the silhouette easier to read. Use the custom color inputs when you want a particular shade, or keep the built-in palette for a coordinated look. Inspect the square preview for overall balance and the circular preview for clipped outer details. A profile platform may apply its own crop, so keeping the important face shapes near the center is a practical final check.
alternative.step3_title: Download, keep a copy and upload it where needed
alternative.step3_body: Press Download 256×256 PNG when you are happy with the result. The file is a static square image you can keep on your device and upload through another platform’s own profile settings. If that service asks for a different size, start from the original export and use the pixel art resizer. For a second mood, keep the colors and hairstyle, change only the expression, then download a separate copy. Upload requirements can change, so check the destination’s guidance if a file is rejected.
alternative.case1_body: Use the editor when you want a readable pixel face for a new account or a refreshed identity. Choose an expression that works at chat-thumbnail size and check the round crop before exporting. A distinctive hairstyle or outfit color can do more for recognition than many small accessories. Keep the downloaded file so you can reuse the same face elsewhere. This tool gives you the image; uploading it and choosing the account crop remain part of the destination platform’s profile settings.
alternative.case2_title: A coordinated set of simple profile pictures
alternative.case2_body: For a club, friend group or small project, give several characters a shared background or outfit palette. Then vary the hair, expression and glasses so each portrait remains distinguishable. The same square composition helps the images sit together in an account grid or member list. Work on one character at a time and download it before changing the next. There is no batch export or stored team collection here, so organize the resulting PNG files yourself with names that make sense to your group.
alternative.case3_title: A game portrait or a craft starting image
alternative.case3_body: A static pixel face can become a player-card portrait, dialogue-box placeholder or starting image for a craft pattern. Choose a transparent background for an interface composition, or a simple solid color for a standalone tile. Export the PNG and continue with the pixel art resizer or pattern maker when the project needs a larger image or a numbered grid. Inspect the result in its intended setting: the avatar editor creates a portrait, not a full-body sprite, movement frames or a finished physical pattern.
alternative.choose_title: Choose the route that matches the result you want
alternative.choose1: Use this page when a simple pixel face is already the right style and you want to move from a preset to a PNG in one editor. The fixed square output removes one formatting decision, and the controls make it easy to compare a few variations. It is particularly practical when you need a temporary profile image, a matching set of compact portraits or a clearly defined character for a prototype. The useful question is whether these visible options can make the image you need.
alternative.choose2: If you want a particular creator’s visual style or exact illustrated parts, use that creator’s Picrew maker. Check its description and permitted uses before working with the resulting image. This editor cannot import a Picrew maker or reproduce its artwork. Treat the two routes as options for different outcomes: one gives you the square pixel face shown here, while the other lets you work within the maker you selected.
alternative.limits_title: Know what this editor can keep and create
alternative.limits1: The current output is one static PNG. There is no animation timeline, freehand pixel canvas, AI prompt box or hosted marketplace of creator-made editors. Hairstyles, expressions and accessories come from the options displayed in the tool. A larger PNG preserves the existing pixel shapes rather than inventing new details. If you want to pixelate a photograph or illustration, use the separate image-to-pixel-art converter; it begins with your uploaded image instead of this character’s editable parts.
alternative.limits2: Keep an exported copy before changing a character you like. The public editor does not save a cloud project, and the downloaded PNG does not contain editable control settings. You can make related variations by changing the current controls, but the tool does not reload a PNG into the original hair and expression choices. If saving editable maker states matters to you, compare that requirement with the tools you are considering. Picrew documents a separate Save feature with its own account and plan conditions.
alternative.faq1_q: Is this an official Picrew tool?
alternative.faq1_a: No. This is our independent square face generator. It uses the pixel character options shown on this page and does not host, copy or import a Picrew creator’s image maker.
alternative.faq2_q: Do I need to register to make an avatar here?
alternative.faq2_a: No account is needed for this editor or its current PNG download. This describes our workflow, not a claim that all Picrew use requires registration. Picrew’s terms also recognize users who are not registered members.
alternative.faq3_q: Can I recreate the Picrew avatar from a shared link?
alternative.faq3_a: Use the maker in the original link if you need that artwork and its specific parts. Here you can create a different square pixel character using our own hairstyles, expressions, colors and accessories.
alternative.faq4_q: Can I download a PNG directly?
alternative.faq4_a: Yes. The button beside the preview exports a 256×256 PNG, with transparency when selected. Picrew also supports image downloads after finishing a maker, so the distinction here is our direct editor-to-file workflow.
alternative.faq5_q: Will the download itself be round?
alternative.faq5_a: The file is square. The round preview is a crop check for profile interfaces that use a circular mask. Important face features should remain visible in both previews before you download.
alternative.faq6_q: Does the editor keep previous characters?
alternative.faq6_a: There is no saved-character gallery or history stack in the current tool. Download a version before randomizing or replacing it. Keep separate files for different expressions or palettes you want to reuse.
alternative.faq7_q: Is it faster than every Picrew maker?
alternative.faq7_a: We have not benchmarked individual Picrew makers. Quick refers to starting from one ready-made pixel face, editing in place and using a direct PNG download. Loading speed also depends on your device and connection.
